objective: Implement a learner-defined Python dataset-gate function and write its required imports in the supplied pipeline's test stage. Author named contract checks and assertions for valid, boundary and invalid fixtures, including a fixture missing a required feature. Preserve tested snapshot identities and failure evidence. Write and reload the existing Cloud Build configuration with PyYAML, inspect its resolved fields, and wire fatal gate execution and explicit training dependencies. Use the configured repository commit trigger and branch filter to run accepted and rejected fixtures.
success: The declared valid and acceptable boundary fixtures pass; invalid fixtures produce named failure evidence and an unsuccessful gate-process exit. Reloaded configuration retains the required image, command, step IDs and waitFor dependencies without permitting required gate failures. Actual triggered-run results show training starts only after an accepted quality stage and never starts after a rejected quality stage. Tested snapshots and failed checks remain available for validation of a repaired dataset against the same contract.

live_code.required_skill: Write a dataset-gate function that aggregates named checks under the supplied policy, test it with assert predicates, and connect its fatal result to the existing Cloud Build test stage.
allowed_syntax: Learner-written imports for declared dataset-reading and validation dependencies
Function calls and local variable assignment
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide the existing authorized repository, commit trigger and branch filter, Cloud Build configuration, declared dependencies, dataset contract, gate policy and dataset snapshot. Include the missing-required-feature fixture described in the example and locations for learner-authored valid, boundary and invalid fixtures. Leave the gate function, imports and assertions unwritten. Retain the existing training entry point without requiring changes to its implementation.
live_code.observable_success: Assertions distinguish the declared fixture cases in ordinary non-optimized execution. Named results determine an explicit gate decision, rejected execution exits unsuccessfully, and saved evidence identifies the tested snapshot and failed requirements. Resolved configuration fields and actual triggered stage results establish that a successful gate permits training while a failed required check prevents training from starting.
